recipes.name: Chicken Massaman Curry
ingredients_raw: 1.25 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast meat - cubed

steps.text: Heat vegetable oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in curry paste and minced ginger; cook and stir for 2 minutes. Add in cubed chicken, and cook until the pieces turn white on the outside, about 3 minutes.

Mix in peanut butter, brown sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind paste, stirring to combine. Add potatoes and coconut milk. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the potatoes are tender and the chicken pieces are no longer pink in the center, about 20 minutes.
Add lime juice and cook for an additional 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Massaman Curry
raw_recipe.description: This massaman curry recipe, flavored with lime, tamarind, and coconut milk, is quick and easy to make. Enjoy the deliciously warm, comforting flavors.

review.reviewBody: Good basic recipe, although you really want to start off frying the paste first with the oil for a couple minutes and then add the creamy part of the coconut milk. Let the two mix better. I also didn't add peanut butter, because I think that's cheating kind of and another user complained about the thickness of the curry (I like mine soupy, too). I would just use peanuts, throwing them in with the potatoes or at the end, and maybe peanut oil to fry it all up with.

I have made this countless times over the last few years and everyone loves it! It is good over rice or just alone in a bowl. For the most part, I follow the directions exactly but I do sub a couple of ingredients. When I began making this, I had trouble finding tamarind paste. So I consulted my Malaysian friend about how best to substitute this. She suggested raisins and a bit of water. I use my immersion blender to make a paste. Also, instead of using white potatoes, I cut up sweet potatoes. It complements this dish well. We will continue to make this over and over. Everyone loves it!

I had a hard time finding some of the ingredients so i substituted a great deal. I had no curry paste and no tamarind paste. 
3 T yellow curry powder
1 t smoked paprika
1 t chili paste
2 T ginger paste
2 T fish sauce
1/2 C peanut butter (i like extra)
2 cans coconut milk
Sweet potatoes instead of regular 
Add 1 whole diced onion
Add 1/2 red pepper diced 
Add 1 C green beans

I cooked my chicken in pan first, i have issues adding raw chicken to my sauces even though i know fully cooked. Then i added potatoes. Then put spices including ginger and in stirred, until fragrant, 15 seconds. Added coconut milk and peanut butter and fish sauce. Simmer 20 minutes. Add onions and green beans in last 5-10 minutes when adding fresh lime juice. While its simmering, make rice. 

Very good, i would definitely make this again!

This was the first time I made curry of any sort (and I am not any kind of master chef, just a college kid) and it turned out perfectly! Two changes: First, I couldn't find tamarind paste so I used Worcestshire sauce. 

Second, I had heard from a couple of people who had cooked curry before that the longer the curry could cook, the better it tastes, so I decided to convert this recipe into a slow-cooker version. 
I sauteed the chicken in the oil and transferred it to the slow-cooker, leaving some oil/juice behind. Poured in one and a half large potatoes and three medium carrots, peeled and chopped. Then I made the curry sauce, combining the other ingredients in the order of the recipe. Poured that over the chicken and vegetables, cooked on high for 3 hours and then on low for 2 hours. Served over jasmine rice, dressed with ripe avocado and cashews. Perfect and tasty meal for a cold night!

I have actually made this a few times and done some lovely variations each time. This is a fun leaping off point for this gorgeous curry. Things that I learnt along the way? Use tamarind concentrate, the real thing made in India if you can. It is gorgeous. I added kafir lime leaves to mine, lovely!!! I used almond butter in mine, very nice! I also used two cans of coconut milk. One in the cooking process, as indicated in the method, and one right at the end a couple of minutes before the lime juice. Don't let the curry come to a boil after that last can goes in. ??

Good recipe.... I too, added carrots and onions, along with some sweet potatoes. Next time I make this I will add some red, yellow and orange bell peppers and some chili paste. I felt like it needed some spicy heat. As this was cooking I added some water to loosen it up a bit.... came out perfect. Served it with brown rice, fresh basil and crushed peanuts.

We really enjoy Thai food and I have been looking for massaman curry recipe for a long time. I could not find massaman curry paste so just used hot curry paste I had. Could not find tamarind paste in the stores here. I actually did not know what it was. I found several suggestions for substitutions . I went with one that called for equal amounts of chopped dried apricots, raisins, lemon juice and prunes but I did not have any. Cover with boiling water and let sit until fruit softened. I then blended it with my hand blender. It made a nice chutney like blend. It was flavourful and smelled great when cooking. I used sweet potatoes,green onions ,carrots and a bit of red pepper. We both enjoyed it and will make again. Probably used a little bit less peanut butter.

This is utter perfection and sooo quick to make! I like to make mine with broccoli and sweet potato, and I cut the fish sauce down to 1 tblsp. I also use 1 tblsp tamarind concentrate instead of tamarind paste cuz it's way less obnoxious to deal with.

I live in Thailand and this is one of my favorite curries! Warm and cinnamon-y! This recipe is very plain, and several things will make it phenomenal-- first use Massaman ( or masman, their English isn't always spelled the same) curry-- normal curry lacks the cinnamon flavor. Essential. This is "Muslim curry" in Thai- so it is supposed to have a regional taste. Second, my Thai friends all make this with broth also-- to match the meat. (Additional to coconut milk.) Third, add carrots ( big Thai veggie!) and onion if you want the street food version. Last, they often add pineapple to this recipe too!! Yum! Love this dish, but needs some upgrades to be quality food that tastes like is made here. Basic recipe as is.

For some reason, I found this pretty salty. We made changes to it, adding lemongrass, ginger and garlic. We also added more veggies: broccoli, red pepper, 2 tomatoes and 2 hot peppers. We also added fewer potatoes and it cooked down a little in order to cook all those vegetables, so that could have been it. Still, great flavour. Did not add the peanut butter as my husband doesn't like that flavour so much. I would like to try it though.

There is simply way too much peanut butter. Instead of being a background flavour to enhance the curry and spice, it blankets it. Also, it should look redder with a tinge of oil.....instead the PB is over powering and makes it look brown. I would switch the PB to one tablespoon.
Maybe too much peanut butter.

I followed this recipe to make dinner for myself and my boyfriend and it ended up way too sour with 3 tablespoons of tamarind paste. We tried adding more coconut milk and sugar to counteract it, and we didn’t have any baking soda on hand so we ended up with a sour and tangy curry.

I made this and even ate it again as left-overs. But it was just OK. Not particularly flavorful and takes a long time to prepare, what with the chopping and mincing and making the tamarind paste. I won't be making it again.
Good, but a bit sour. Next time I’ll cut back to half the tamarind paste, and ended up adding a 4th TBSP brown sugar to sweeten a bit. Left out the lime altogether.
Recipe was great! I added a dash of cinnamon. Came out really good!

Wanted to learn to make this after my fiance tried it at a Thai restaurant and, no joke, this tasted EXACTLY like where we ordered from! The only change I made was to add a teaspoon of sesame seed oil. I did it the first time simply because I was missing some peanut butter, but then when I made it again without, I did find myself missing it so I recommend the addition if you have it.
Excellent

Made this without the peanut butter, used raw cashews added mixed Asian stir fry that i had on hand , and ditched the potatoe. Cubed up a couple of firm Avacados instead and tossed them in just as I was taking the wok off the heat. Spiced it up with some chili garlic paste. Delish! 5 stars for the way mine turned out
One of the best Massaman Currys I've ever had!
